title: UPF keeps sending GTP Tunnel Downlink traffic to the IP address of first gNodeB the UE did ATTACH on, even when UE is moving between gNodeBs
body:
In my lab I have a setup of 2 X Airspan gNodeBs AirSpeed 2900 (from the list of "tested gNodeB with Open5Gs").
gNodeB #1 has IP address ending with 225, and gNodeB #2 has IP address ending with 221.
I am doing the following sequence:
Step 1) ATTACH 5G UE on gNodeB #1 --> this is successful and UE receives IP address of 10.45.0.8 (configured for this UE in Open5Gs webGUI)
Step 2) Initiate ping to 10.45.0.8 from the Open5Gs machine itself. This means ping from 10,45,0,1 (ogstun) to 10.45.0.8 --> ping is successful, UE replies to the ping.
Step 3) UE sends 5G-NAS "Deregistration Request" to Open5Gs which is successful.
Step 4) Attenuate RF signal of gNodeB #1 so RF signal of gNodeB #2 becomes much stronger
Step 5) ATTACH 5G UE on gNodeB #2 --> this is successful and UE receives IP address of 10.45.0.8 (configured for this UE in Open5Gs webGUI)
Step 6) Initiate ping to 10.45.0.8 from the Open5Gs machine itself. This means ping from 10,45,0,1 (ogstun) to 10.45.0.8 --> ping FAILS there is NO response from UE.
Looking at the wirshark capture I can see that the GTP Tunnel encapsulating the {Ping from 10.45.0.1 to 10.45.0.8} is actually being sent to IP address ending with 225 which is gNodeB #1 instead of IP address ending with 221 which is gNodeB #2.
The UE did a full DETACH from gNodeB #1 and NEW ATTACH to gNodeB #2 so it is not clear why the UPF still remembers the gNodeB #1 IP address for this UE GTP Downlink traffic.
It doesn't matter how many times I do for the UE the DETACH/ATTACH - the Open5Gs UPF is constantly sending the Downlink GTP Tunnel to the IP address of the FIRST gNodeB the UE did ATTACH to. 
The only way to get out of this situation is to restart the services of the Open5Gs so the Open5Gs will forget the IP address of the first gNodeB that the UE did ATTACH to.

The same behaviour from UPF occurs also if UE went to IDLE (user-inactivity) on gNodeB #1 and did Service Request on gNodeB #2. 
The UPF still sends GTP Downlink traffic to IP address of gNodeB #1

The same behaviour from UPF occurs also after 5G Handover (5G NG-AP Handover and 5G Xn-AP Handover). Even though the 5G Handover is successful, the UPF continues to send the GTP Downlink traffic to the IP address of the Source gNodeB.
